paper_metadata.title: Strengthening and dynamic recrystallization mediated by Si-alloying in a refractory high entropy alloy

evidence.quote: Refractory high entropy alloys (RHEAs) are increasingly attractive for potential high temperature applications.
In this work, the effects of Si alloying on the microstructure, mechanical properties and hot deformation behavior of a refractory HEA (TaMo0.5NbZrTi1.5Al0.1) is investigated.
The TaMo0.5NbZrTi1.5Al0.1 and TaMo0.5NbZrTi1.5Al0.1Si0.1 (at.%) alloys were fabricated using a non-consumable arc melting furnace, denoted as RHEA and Si-RHEA, respectively.

A high vacuum heat treatment furnace was used to carry out the annealing treatment at 1300 °C. The annealing time was 48 h and the whole process was protected by argon atmosphere.

The work suggests that Si-alloying can be an effective approach for significantly enhancing strength and deformation compatibility of RHEAs at room and elevated temperatures by enabling the formation of fine silicides and the additional solute effects.
